_what: The exemption register RFC-2026-016 §4 made the replacement for "force RLS where compatible".
_why: "Where compatible" was retired for being unfalsifiable: no artefact could be pointed at to decide whether a table met it. A register is the falsifiable form -- an exemption either has a row here or it does not exist.

It is read in BOTH directions, which is what makes it a control rather than a list. A table that is not forced and has no row is refused. A row whose exemption is not visible in the catalog is refused too, because a register that keeps rows for exemptions nobody took is a register nobody can trust to be complete.

It was mandated on 2026-09-05 and did not exist until 2026-09-06. A1's countersignature §5.1 found the gap: the phrase was retired for being unfalsifiable and its replacement was unfalsifiable by absence.

_shape.role: the role the exemption is for -- a role name, or "*" when the exemption is the table not being forced at all
_shape.table: unqualified table name in the app schema
_shape.reason: why the general rule cannot hold here, in a sentence someone can disagree with
_shape.owner: the run or human accountable for removing it
_shape.review_date: ISO date. An exemption past its review date is a finding, not a grandfathered fact.
